Emerald Siam Energy Confirms Expansion of Gas Processing Facilities in Eastern Thailand

Emerald Siam Energy has announced a significant investment to expand its natural gas processing capacity in Rayong province, a move that underscores the steady growth of Thailand’s oil and gas producers sector. The company stated on Wednesday that it will allocate an estimated 4.2 billion baht (approximately US$115 million) to construct a new processing train at its existing facility, targeting completion by the end of 2026.

The expansion is expected to boost Emerald Siam Energy’s total processing capacity by 20%, supporting rising domestic demand from power generation and industrial customers. “This investment reflects our commitment to ensuring energy security for Thailand as the country’s needs continue to evolve,” said Chaiwat Srisuk, Chief Executive Officer of Emerald Siam Energy. “The additional train will enable us to deliver cleaner and more reliable natural gas to our downstream partners.”

According to the Petroleum Institute of Thailand, domestic consumption of natural gas has grown steadily at around 3% annually over the past five years, with the Eastern Economic Corridor driving much of the recent demand. “Investments like this are essential for sustaining industrial growth in the region,” commented Dr. Orasa Kanchanaporn, energy analyst at Bangkok Futures Research. “They also align with Thailand’s policy to increase the role of natural gas in the national energy mix.”

The expansion project is expected to create approximately 500 construction jobs at peak and provide additional opportunities for local suppliers. Emerald Siam Energy said it will work closely with provincial authorities and community leaders to minimize environmental impacts and ensure a safe construction process.

Industry observers note that the investment signals continued confidence in Thailand’s oil and gas sector, even as the government encourages a gradual transition toward renewable energy sources.
